newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Unions seek breaking of Canberra labour deal.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Unions seek breaking of Canberra labour deal.

text.p: Australian Council of Trade Unions (ACTU) president Jennie George said on Monday she would pressure the Australian Democrats to break their agreement with the government on labour reforms.
"I'm here for the next two weeks to try and get it better, to try and get further progress," George told reporters.

Asked if she wanted Democrats leader Cheryl Kernot to break the written agreement, she said: "Yes. I'm going to be asking in areas where I believe the agreement does not conform ... on the basis of my negotiations with her, for her to have another look."

George said she applauded the Democrats for the improvements they had already made to the Workplace Relations bill, although some areas such as age-based regulations and youth wages still needed work. "The amendments that have been secured by the Democrats in their negotiations with the government have improved the original bill," she said.

"Over the next week or two, it is the intention of the ACTU and the union movement to try and make those changes better. But at the end of the day, this is not our legislation and we do not support it in any form," she said.
